decision: This plan exists because plan 2026-06-06-001 D018 deferred browser-originated governed mutation. v0 ships a read-only workbench (copy/handoff); this plan owns the executor trust boundary so the UX plan stays clean.

Threat-model-first: every feature neutralizes one risk of a browser-driven local executor (unauthorized invocation, scope creep, partial/duplicate mutation, tampered history, stale tab). The command allowlist is bound to operator_bucket actions only — never a general shell.
Demand-gated: do not build until the 2026-06-06-001 read-only workbench is in use and the copy/handoff loop is demonstrably the friction. status:draft until then.

Embedded terminal is its OWN capability (the execution plane for GUI+agents), formalized as the T-series (T1-T4) expansion of this plan — NOT mixed into operator-console F007/F008/F009. Built stdlib-only (pty_bridge hand-rolled WS+PTY; threaded serve). Governance per operator checklist: --enable-terminal OFF by default; loopback+Origin+per-serve-token; audit line when armed; visible UI warning+scope; NO auto-enable from config/build; threat-model-embedded-terminal.md with residual-risk disclosure (local same-user process can read the localhost token — inherent to localhost terminals). Tests: 14 py (bridge handshake/framing/PTY/resize + serve off-by-default/token/origin/loopback/audit/no-auto-enable) + 3 vitest dock smoke. The original F001-F004 governed-action-button channel remains draft/unbuilt. Branch chore/plan-ledger-reconciliation-2026-06-04 UNMERGED.

Serve-reliability fix (F009): the reported 'fleet build hangs on QuantRE / serve unreliable' was a MISDIAGNOSIS — fleet build is ~1.3s and clean serve binds in ~5s incl. QuantRE (proven via faulthandler-timed build + serve --once). Real defect: DEFAULT_PORT=0 made `dashboard serve` pick a RANDOM ephemeral port each run, so the operator couldn't find it and a stale static server on 8787 showed the pre-plan bundle. Fix per operator choice 'stable 8787, fail loud on conflict': CLI --port now defaults to DEFAULT_CLI_PORT=8787 (internal serve_start/test default stays 0=ephemeral); EADDRINUSE on a chosen port → REFUSED rc=2 with port_conflict_message naming the holder (lsof+ps, best-effort) + `--port N` remediation; generic OSError keeps bind-failed rc=1. 7 new port-policy tests; singleton serve --once test pinned to --port 0 for hermeticity. No build-speed work needed.

title: Ledger reconciliation: terminal half shipped, button-channel half intentionally demand-gated
decision: Reconciling the ledger state so active-with-4-open-features is not mistaken for stalled work. The embedded-terminal T-series (F005-F009) is SHIPPED and passing (PTY<->WebSocket bridge, serve integration, governance/threat-model, frontend dock, serve-port reliability). The browser-originated governed-action button-channel (F001-F004: local action backend + gate approve/reject + safe-tier apply + idempotency) remains passes:false BY DESIGN per D003 — deliberately demand-gated until the copy/handoff loop proves to be the actual operator friction. The plan stays status:active as the legitimate owner of that deferred executor-channel capability; F001-F004 are a valid future increment, not work-in-flight. No build, no status flip, no paid call — this is a ledger annotation. To actually build F001-F004 later requires an explicit un-gate decision (re-evaluating D003's trigger) before lock + dispatch.
rationale: Per the plans-vs-operator-actions + demand-driven-v2 discipline: a plan can correctly stay active while holding deliberately-deferred features; the ledger should record that the deferral is intentional so the open features aren't read as stuck.
